title: Page Object Model
summary: Write a LoginPage page object (locators + goto + login) and use it in a positive and a negative login test.
why: When the login form changes, you fix one class instead of 40 tests. Page objects also make tests read like your manual steps: loginPage.login(user, password).
objectives: class LoginPage with locators created once in the constructor
Two tests that create new LoginPage(page)
hints: Keep assertions in tests, not in page objects (except small helpers).
Expose locators (loginPage.error) so tests can assert on them.
pitfalls: Putting expect() everywhere inside the page object — failures become harder to read.
Creating locators inside every method instead of once.
teachAlong: Cause: locators live in one class.
Effect: UI changes are a one-line fix.
Gate: requires new LoginPage(page) and catches a wrong redirect.

requires.reason: The task requires the page object: create it with new LoginPage(page) in your tests.

mutants.reason: after sign-in the app goes to the home page instead of the dashboard
the dashboard greets the user as 'Guest'

wrongSolutions.label: no page object
